## Code Review

This pull request introduces scaffolding for parallel advanced parsing engines for Cisco ASA (using `ciscoconfparse`) and FortiGate (using `fortios-xutils`), enabled via a new `--use-external-engines` CLI flag. It adds the new parser modules, updates configuration loading and path-checking logic to route requests to these engines, adds external dependencies to `pyproject.toml`, and includes unit tests for the new scaffolding. Feedback on the changes highlights several issues: missing `Any` imports in type hints across multiple files, unused `socket` imports in the new advanced parser modules, and the use of bare `except:` clauses in `advanced_parser.py` which should be replaced with specific exception handling.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces scaffolding for parallel "advanced" parsing engines for Cisco ASA and FortiGate configurations using external libraries (ciscoconfparse and fortios-xutils). It adds a new `--use-external-engines` CLI flag, defines the `AdvancedASAConfig` and `AdvancedFTGConfig` classes, updates the loader and inspection modules to route requests to these advanced parsers when enabled, and includes corresponding unit tests. Feedback on the changes highlights a missing import of `Any` in `parsers/cisco/asa/inspect.py` and a bare `except:` clause in `parsers/cisco/asa/advanced_parser.py` that should catch `ValueError` specifically.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces scaffolding and routing for parallel, advanced parsing engines for Cisco ASA (using `ciscoconfparse`) and FortiGate (using `fortios-xutils`), enabled via a new `--use-external-engines` CLI flag. It also includes corresponding documentation updates, dependency definitions, and unit tests. Feedback on the changes suggests replacing a bare `except:` clause with a specific `except ValueError:` in the advanced ASA parser, and resolving a type hint issue in the ASA inspection module where `Any` is referenced without being imported.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces scaffolding for parallel advanced parsing engines for Cisco ASA and FortiGate configurations, leveraging external libraries (ciscoconfparse and fortios-xutils). It adds the --use-external-engines CLI flag, integrates the new AdvancedASAConfig and AdvancedFTGConfig classes into the loader and inspection flows, defines the external dependency group in pyproject.toml, and adds corresponding unit tests. Feedback on the changes includes addressing a cycle-detection bug in resolve_service_group where visited.discard(name) was omitted, replacing a bare except: block with a specific ValueError catch, and resolving a missing Any import in type hints by using object instead.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces scaffolding for parallel advanced parsing engines for Cisco ASA and FortiGate configurations using external libraries (ciscoconfparse and fortios-xutils), enabled via a new --use-external-engines CLI flag. The feedback identifies critical bugs in the cycle resolution and caching logic of resolve_network and resolve_service_group in the advanced ASA parser, which can lead to permanently caching incomplete results. Additionally, incorrect test fixture paths in tests/test_external_engines.py and a missing import of Any in parsers/cisco/asa/inspect.py need to be resolved to prevent test and runtime failures.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces scaffolding for parallel, advanced parsing engines powered by external libraries (ciscoconfparse and fortios-xutils) for Cisco ASA and FortiGate configurations, enabled via a new --use-external-engines CLI flag. It also enhances cycle-handling logic in the legacy ASA parser to prevent caching of incomplete results. Feedback on the changes highlights a missing import of Any in inspect.py (recommending a string literal type hint instead), a mismatch in cycle-handling logic in the new AdvancedASAConfig.resolve_network method, and incorrect fixture paths in the newly added unit tests.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces scaffolding for parallel advanced parsing engines powered by external libraries (`ciscoconfparse` and `fortios-xutils`) for Cisco ASA and FortiGate, accessible via the new `--use-external-engines` CLI flag. It also updates the legacy ASA parser to correctly handle and invalidate cached cyclic network object-groups. Feedback on these changes highlights that the new `AdvancedASAConfig.resolve_network` method is missing the cycle-handling logic implemented in the legacy parser, and that `Any` is used in type annotations in `parsers/cisco/asa/inspect.py` without being imported, which will cause static analysis failures.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces scaffolding and integration for parallel "advanced" parsing engines using external libraries (`ciscoconfparse` for Cisco ASA and `fortios-xutils` for FortiGate), controlled by a new `--use-external-engines` CLI flag. It also updates the cycle-detection and caching logic in the legacy ASA parser to handle incomplete resolutions safely, adds documentation and roadmaps, and includes corresponding unit tests.

Feedback on the changes:
- In `parsers/cisco/asa/inspect.py` and `parsers/fortigate/inspect.py`, the fallback logic only catches `NotImplementedError` but should also catch `ImportError` to gracefully handle cases where the optional external dependencies are not installed.
- In both `AdvancedASAConfig` and `AdvancedFTGConfig` (`advanced_parser.py`), since the advanced engines are not yet implemented, raising `NotImplementedError` immediately after the import check would prevent unnecessary data structure initialization and overhead.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces scaffolding for parallel, AST-based advanced parsing engines using external libraries (ciscoconfparse and fortios-xutils), enabled via the experimental --use-external-engines CLI flag. It updates the CLI, loader, documentation, and dependencies, and adds unit tests for the new scaffolding. Additionally, the PR implements cycle-aware caching in the legacy ASA parser's service group and network resolution methods. The reviewer identified an issue in the network resolution cache logic where the resolved network object group is not cached before returning, which leads to redundant resolutions and renders the cache eviction logic for cyclic groups ineffective; a code suggestion was provided to address this.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces scaffolding for parallel, AST-based advanced parsing engines using external libraries (ciscoconfparse and fortios-xutils), enabled via a new --use-external-engines CLI flag. It refactors config loading to use a centralized _get_engine helper, updates inspection and path-checking functions to support the new engines, improves cycle handling in ASA service group and network resolution, and adds corresponding unit tests and documentation. Feedback on the changes highlights an issue in cli/access-list-inspector.py where directly instantiating AdvancedASAConfig bypasses the centralized _get_engine helper and its uniform error handling, potentially swallowing errors silently; using _get_engine with explicit error handling is recommended.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces scaffolding and CLI support (`--use-external-engines`) for parallel, AST-based advanced parsing engines using `ciscoconfparse` (for Cisco ASA) and `fortios-xutils` (for FortiGate). It also refactors the legacy ASA parser to improve cycle detection and cache cleanup for nested network and service object-groups, alongside adding comprehensive unit tests. Feedback on the changes highlights a performance issue in `resolve_network` where resolved network object groups are returned directly without being cached in `self._network_cache`, rendering the cache cleanup logic a no-op.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces scaffolding for an experimental, AST-based parallel parsing engine using external libraries (ciscoconfparse and fortios-xutils), integrated via a new --use-external-engines CLI flag and a centralized get_engine loader. It also enhances the legacy ASA parser with robust cycle detection for network and service object-groups, fixes a typo in the --singularity CLI flag, and adds corresponding unit tests. The review feedback highlights that get_engine should normalize vendor strings to lowercase for robustness, and notes that several inspection and comparison modules still directly instantiate legacy config classes, bypassing the new engine. The reviewer recommends updating these functions to accept and propagate the use_external_engines parameter.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces scaffolding for parallel, AST-based advanced parsing engines using `ciscoconfparse` and `fortios-xutils`, enabled via the `--use-external-engines` flag. It refactors configuration loading in `parsers/loader.py` to support engine selection with graceful fallback, and improves cycle detection and cache management in ASA network and service object-group resolution. Additionally, the CLI adds a `--singularity` alias, and new tests are introduced to cover these changes. The review feedback highlights a critical issue in `cli/access-list-inspector.py` where using `load_config` to map to IR attempts to re-read from `args.config`, which fails when reading from stdin (`"-"`) because the stream has already been consumed; the reviewer suggests using `get_engine` directly with the pre-loaded configuration text instead.
